standard.title: Miner's Safety Goggles — Specification (खनिकों के लिये सुरक्षा चश्मे — विशिष्टि)
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the material specifications, design configurations, dimensions, safety requirements, and testing protocols for safety goggles used by miners to protect eyes against hazards such as mechanical impact from flying rock chips and fine dust particles encountered during mining operations.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes the material specifications, design configurations, dimensions, safety requirements, and testing protocols for safety goggles used by miners to protect eyes against hazards such as mechanical impact from flying rock chips and fine dust particles encountered during mining operations.

supersedes: None (Developed as a dedicated personal protective equipment standard specifically optimized for the mining sector's harsh mechanical and environmental conditions)

relationships.description: References IS 4355 : 1977 for material specifications or material-related requirements.
References IS 2 : 1960 for rules on rounding numerical values and reported measurements.
Relates to IS 14489 : 2018 as an allied product standard covering a similar or complementary product.
Relates to IS 18001 : 2007 as an allied product standard covering a similar or complementary product.
Relates to IS 800 : 2007 as an allied product standard covering a similar or complementary product.

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' directly on the packaging of miner's safety goggles or the component itself to certify material quality and safety compliance in the mining market.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, observed dimensions, or physical properties must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The goggle frame must be of sound construction and made of durable plastic or other suitable materials capable of resisting mechanical impacts and prolonged moisture exposure.
The head-band material must be sweat-resistant, non-irritant, and shall not cause skin disease under prolonged shifts.

Lenses must be fabricated from plastic materials, toughened or laminated glass, or a combination of these materials. Untreated glass is strictly prohibited unless backed by plastic or laminated glass to prevent shattering.

Goggles required for use in underground mines shall have no metal parts made of aluminium, magnesium, titanium, or their alloys to prevent light-metal frictional sparking in explosive methane or coal dust atmospheres.

Goggles are classified into Type A (Cup-type, with two eye-pieces connected across the nose with adjustment arrangements) and Type B (Box-type, providing total enclosure of both eyes with either separate lens holders or a single continuous window lens).
Lenses for Type A goggles must be circular with a nominal diameter of 50 ± 2 mm.
Type B goggles fitted with separate lens holders must have circular lenses of 50 ± 2 mm in diameter.

Type B goggles fitted with a single-piece window lens must feature two symmetrically spaced circular viewing fields, each with a minimum diameter of 52 mm, with their centers spaced exactly 62 mm apart measured horizontally in the front plane as worn.
The head-band must have a minimum width of 10 mm to distribute pressure evenly and prevent slipping.
